create issue (WORKING RECIPE, confirmed 2026-09-25 again): jq --arg/$var gets falsely flagged by the sandbox's shell-expansion detector even inside single-quoted jq filters - AVOID entirely, bake literal strings into the jq filter. Also avoid heredoc bodies (`cat <<'EOF' > file` inside a single Bash call) - flagged as unstaticaly-analyzable file_redirect even with zero shell variables present; use the Write tool to create the body file instead, THEN run jq -Rs over it in a separate Bash call. Full recipe: (1) Write tool -> eslint-factory/.tmp_issueN_body.md (inside repo working dir only, NOT /tmp/gh-aw/*). (2) `jq -Rs '{title: "literal text", body: ., labels: ["eslint","eslint-factory"]}' eslint-factory/.tmp_issueN_body.md > eslint-factory/.tmp_issueN.json`. (3) `safeoutputs create_issue . < eslint-factory/.tmp_issueN.json`. (4) rm both temp files, confirm `git status --short eslint-factory/` is clean.

create_discussion params: title*, body*, category, integrity, secrecy.

For a rule with 100+ importing/call-site files, the productive strategy is: read the rule's OWN helper functions for internal asymmetries first, THEN grep the corpus only for the specific shapes that asymmetry predicts.

Cross-file same-name variables are IRRELEVANT to any bare-name-keyed rule's scope-blindness, since ESLint's create(context) runs fresh per file - only same-FILE name collisions across different scopes actually trigger a scope-blind bug.

Small/rare-shape findings (e.g. a real logic gap with only 2-3 live call sites, all currently correct) do not meet the historical 'broadly applicable idiom' filing bar - document as a retained-but-not-filed theory in nextPriorities instead of forcing an issue.

A rule's own .test.ts file is authoritative for whether a behavior is a known/intended limitation vs an undiscovered bug - always check the test file before filing an issue about a suspected gap, even if live-corpus grounding looks strong.

Issues auto-expire (~1wk TTL) and get bot-closed as not_planned - a single expiry is NOT reliably 'unfixed housekeeping': #61044/#61543 both expired AND were genuinely fixed in the same window (3 confirmed instances total now). ALWAYS re-read the current rule source (not just memory's cached description) before deciding to refile an expired item - the fix may have already landed.

Bash sandbox flags multi-command chains, xargs, sort, printf-with-newlines, and some grep -E patterns as 'contains expansion'/'multiple operations requiring approval' even with zero actual shell variables - prefer the Grep/Glob/Read tools over Bash for exploratory searching; reserve Bash for single simple gh/git one-liners.
